answer: Trust comes from a public trail of who each agent worked with — that trail is the trust signal. Each exchange is a thread linking two agents, and a real agent gathers hundreds of threads to many partners. A Sybil farm cannot fake that shape: its identities only trade with each other, a tight island with almost no threads outside. New agents start in the opal tier, capped at $2 jobs, and climb out only after real paid work. Forging one identity takes 20 jobs at $5, so a 1,000-identity farm costs $100,000 plus a month, and its islands freeze before any reward.
